title: Chat docs
intro: Chat is the chat of your own website and admin: a ready chat widget (or your own chat screens on the visitor API), AI replies with your own AI provider key, knowledge, tools, handoff to your staff, an inbox for your admin, leads, flows and reports. Every conversation, message, lead and knowledge entry is kept in your own database (Connections). Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, AI key and providers, so the chats made there are real. There is no test mode.
visitorApi: Headless: build your own chat screens on the visitor API with the browser token (Authorization: Bearer). A visitor is a guest or a signed-in Accounts user. The first message of a guest answers guestKey: keep it on the device (localStorage, not cookies or URLs) and send it with every request in the SS-Guest header. A signed-in visitor's Accounts sign-in goes in the SS-Sign-In header; when a device sends both, the guest's open chat moves to the account. GET /v1/chat?after=<seq> answers the chat and the messages after a sequence number. Check for new messages from the browser with back-off: every 10 s while the window is open and the tab visible, every 20 s after 5 idle minutes, none after 15 idle minutes or while the tab is hidden, and every 3 s for 45 s while an AI reply is pending (aiPending). There are no websockets.
signedIn: Signed-in chat trusts Accounts sign-ins only: paste your website's Accounts server token into Connections, then pass the visitor's sign-in to the widget with SSChat.identify(token) and call SSChat.identify(null) on sign-out. Chat verifies the sign-in offline with your Accounts public keys. Visitors signed in only to your own login chat as guests.
guests: Guests can send a set number of messages per conversation (default 5, 0 = no limit); at the limit they see Sign in to continue (with Signed-in chat and a sign-in page set), Leave your contact and we will reply (with Lead capture) or Message limit reached.
ai: AI replies use your own key: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible service (base URL and key), with the model you choose, and a backup provider when the main one fails. Answers follow Chat's built-in neutral instructions, your business name and contact from business.json, your own instructions (AI instructions, up to 12,000 characters) and knowledge from the features that are on. AI token caps (daily and monthly, in your business time zone) stop AI replies at the cap; AI cost alerts e-mail your staff alert recipients once a month when the month crosses the share you set. The language lock makes the AI answer in the visitor's language. By default AI replies carry the AI assistant label.
knowledge: The knowledge base holds FAQ entries and articles; website pages are fetched when you add them and when you press Fetch again, never on a schedule. Edit them in the knowledge editor widget or with the server API.
tools: Webhook tools are defined in Settings → Tools (name, description, typed parameters, https URL, and whether to send the signed-in visitor's id and e-mail). The AI may call them; Chat sends each call as a POST with a JSON body { tool, arguments, conversationId, visitor? } and the header ss-chat-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>"> made with your tool signing secret (Settings → Tools: reveal, copy, regenerate). Calls time out after 8 seconds and at most 64 kB of the answer is read.
booking: Book-a-slot calls your own booking endpoint (Settings → Tools), signed like a tool call, with two requests: { action: "list_slots", from: "YYYY-MM-DD", to: "YYYY-MM-DD", timeZone } answered with { slots: [{ id, start, end }] }, and { action: "book", slotId, name, email, phone, conversationId } answered with { booked: true, reference? }.
handoff: Handoff moves a chat to a person: the visitor asks (button or phrases), a keyword matches, the AI decides, or the AI fails a number of times in a row. The chat is flagged Waiting for a person and the AI stops until a staff member replies (unless staff paused the AI for that chat). Outside your office hours the visitor is told when staff are back. A guest with no contact details is asked for them.
flows: Flows are short scripted step lists (message, question with buttons, collect a field, hand off, end), started by a page rule (the widget starts them when the chat opens on a matching page, or after the delay) or by a keyword in a visitor message. Path patterns: an exact path, * = one segment, ** = any (for example /products/**).
alerts: Staff alerts, transcripts and AI cost alerts are e-mails sent through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections and write these templates (e-mail) in Notifications. Without it, those answer notifications_not_connected. Alerts link to your Inbox address with ?conversation=<id>. A transcript carries the most recent 1,000 characters of the chat (the longest value Notifications takes).
attachments: Attachments go from the browser straight to your own S3-compatible storage with a short presigned PUT that fixes the type and size; Chat keeps only the object key. Allow your website's origin (and your admin's) in the bucket's CORS: methods PUT and GET, header content-type. Images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF) show inline; PDFs are downloads; nothing else is allowed. The largest file is a setting (default 5 MB, at most 10 MB).
dataRights: Data rights: paste this website's Chat server token into Accounts. Export returns a person's conversations (with their messages and attachments' names) and leads; delete removes them, guest chats merged into the account included. Chat never deletes conversations because of their age; you delete them with DELETE /v1/conversations/<id>.
activity: Activity log: every staff action through the widgets or the server API (reply, note, status, assignment, knowledge edits …) is kept in your database and copied to Accounts when its token is pasted (who, what, target and when — never message contents).
shop: Shop tools, track shipment and product cards come with Ecommerce. These are the Ecommerce routes they will call with the pasted Ecommerce token (Ecommerce implements exactly these):
install: Add the script to the pages of your website. The chat widget mounts itself; it renders nothing while Visitor chat is off, the product is stopped, or your database is not connected.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: Inbox (inbox.read to see conversations and set your presence, inbox.reply to reply and attach, inbox.manage for status, assignment, notes, saved replies, custom field values and max chats), Knowledge editor (knowledge.edit) and Reports (reports.read). Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time. SSChat.onUnread(callback) gives the unread count for your own menu; the server can read it with GET /v1/inbox/unread.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Every route answers JSON; errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.
